title: How to Run Your Own AI Model Router with 9router
summary: Run 9router as a self-hosted AI model router: install with npm or Docker, verify models with curl, connect coding tools, and secure the OpenAI-compatible API.
body_markdown:
9router is an open-source, MIT-licensed routing proxy that runs on your own machine or server and puts every AI provider you connect behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint at` http://localhost:20128/v1` .


If you use Claude Code in one terminal, Cline in your editor and the OpenAI SDK in a side project, you probably have three sets of keys and three base URLs, and each tool needs its own config change whenever you switch models. 9router replaces that with a single local endpoint. This guide covers installing it with npm or Docker, checking it with curl, pointing your tools at it, and locking it down before anything outside localhost can reach it.


## Key Takeaways


- 9router installs with` npm install -g 9router` and starts with` 9router` . The dashboard and the OpenAI-compatible API both listen on port 20128 by default.
- A` GET` request to` http://localhost:20128/v1/models` lists every model and combo the router can serve, so it is the fastest way to check that a provider is connected.
- A combo is a named, ordered list of models that you pass as the` model` value. The router moves to the next model when the current one runs out of quota, gets rate-limited or returns an error.
- If` INITIAL_PASSWORD` is not set, the first dashboard login uses` 123456` . Set your own password and keep the dashboard’s “Require API key” setting on before exposing the instance beyond localhost.


## What Is 9router?


9router is a self-hosted proxy that accepts OpenAI-format requests, routes them to whichever upstream provider you have configured, and translates between OpenAI, Claude and Gemini request formats as needed. The project README lists 40+ supported providers, and the CLI ships as the[9router npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/9router) .


The main difference between 9router and OpenRouter is where the router runs. OpenRouter is a hosted service that you send requests to. 9router is software that you run yourself, and OpenRouter appears in its provider list, so you can put an OpenRouter account behind your own router.


OpenRouter 9router


Where it runs Vendor’s cloud Your machine or server


Who holds provider credentials The service, behind one OpenRouter key Your local 9router instance


Base URL for tools` https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`` http://localhost:20128/v1`


## Why Run a Self-Hosted Model Router


A local router gives every tool the same endpoint and keeps provider credentials in one place, so you can change models without touching tool configs or application code.


- **One endpoint.** Every OpenAI-compatible client uses the same base URL.
- **Keys in one place.** You add provider accounts once, in the dashboard. Each tool only needs a 9router API key.
- **Model switching by string.** Changing models means changing the` model` value and nothing else.
- **Combos.** A combo is a named, ordered list of models that you use as the model name. When the first model runs out of quota, gets rate-limited (429) or returns an error, the router tries the next one.


The usual pattern is to put your preferred model first and cheaper models after it. To compare per-token prices before you choose the fallbacks, use the[LLM API cost calculator](https://openreplay.com/tools/llm-cost-calculator/) .


## How to Install and Run 9router


9router installs as a global npm CLI with` npm install -g 9router` and starts with the` 9router` command. The server listens on port 20128.


```text
npm   install   -g   9router
9router
# Dashboard: http://localhost:20128
# API:       http://localhost:20128/v1
```


If you don’t want a global install,` npx 9router` runs it once.


To run it in Docker, use the[official decolua/9router image](https://hub.docker.com/r/decolua/9router) , which is also published at` ghcr.io/decolua/9router` :


```text
docker   run   -d   --name   9router   \
-p   20128:20128   \
-v   "  $HOME  /.9router:/app/data  "   \
-e   DATA_DIR=/app/data   \
-e   INITIAL_PASSWORD=  '  change-me  '   \
decolua/9router:latest
```


The volume mount keeps the SQLite database (` /app/data/db/data.sqlite` inside the container) when the container restarts. New releases come out often and the` latest` tag moves with them, so pin a specific version tag if you need reproducible deploys.


After 9router starts, finish setup in the dashboard:


1. Open` http://localhost:20128` and log in to the dashboard.
2. Add at least one provider account.
3. Create an API key for your tools.


## Verify the Router with curl


The quickest way to verify that 9router is working is a` GET` request to` /v1/models` , sent before you configure any tool. The response is a JSON list of every model and combo the router can serve, in the standard OpenAI list format.


```text
curl   http://localhost:20128/v1/models
```


The model list answers without a key. Chat requests are different: the dashboard’s “Require API key” setting is on by default, so they need a key from the dashboard. Sending the key with the model list request is a good habit too, because a key that is limited to certain models only sees those models:


```text
curl   http://localhost:20128/v1/models   \
-H   "  Authorization: Bearer   $NINE_ROUTER_API_KEY  "
```


If a model ID from your provider shows up in the list, routing works. If the list is empty, the provider is not connected yet.


## Point Your Tools at 9router


Any client that accepts a custom OpenAI base URL can use 9router. Set the base URL to` http://localhost:20128/v1` and supply an API key created in the dashboard.


### OpenAI SDK


```text
import   OpenAI   from   "  openai  "  ;


const   client   =   new   OpenAI  ({
baseURL  :   "  http://localhost:20128/v1  "  ,
apiKey  :   process  .  env  .  NINE_ROUTER_API_KEY  ,   // created in the 9router dashboard
});


const   res   =   await   client  .  chat  .  completions  .  create  ({
model  :   "  <an id or combo name from /v1/models>  "  ,
messages  :   [{   role  :   "  user  "  ,   content  :   "  Say hello  "   }],
});
console  .  log  (  res  .  choices  [  0  ].  message  .  content  );
```


To switch to another model or a combo, change the` model` string. Nothing else in the code changes.


### Coding Agents


In Cline, choose **OpenAI Compatible** as the[API provider](https://docs.cline.bot/provider-config/openai-compatible) and fill in three values: the base URL` http://localhost:20128/v1` , your dashboard API key, and a model ID copied from` /v1/models` . Terminal agents that let you bring your own provider, such as[OpenCode](https://blog.openreplay.com/opencode-ai-coding-agent/) , take the same three values.


### Pi with pi-9router-ext


The[pi-9router-ext extension](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pi-9router-ext) connects the Pi coding agent to 9router through two environment variables:


```text
pi   install   npm:pi-9router-ext
NINE_ROUTER_BASE_URL  =  http://localhost:20128   NINE_ROUTER_API_KEY  =<  key  >   pi
# inside Pi:
/9router-models
```


When it starts, the extension reads chat models from` /v1/models` . In the 0.2.4 release, it also queries` /v1/models/web` to find 9router’s web search and fetch routes. Run` /9router-models` inside Pi to see what it found.


## How Do You Secure 9router Before Exposing It?


To secure 9router before another machine can reach it, set a dashboard password and the JWT and API key secrets, and leave “Require API key” switched on. The defaults are fine on localhost, but not beyond it. If` INITIAL_PASSWORD` is not set, the first dashboard login uses` 123456` until a password is saved. Set these values from the[official .env.example](https://github.com/decolua/9router/blob/master/.env.example) before you open a port or deploy to a public host:


```text
INITIAL_PASSWORD  =<  long-random-string  >     # first login otherwise uses 123456
JWT_SECRET  =<  long-random-string  >           # listed under "Required" in .env.example
API_KEY_SECRET  =<  long-random-string  >       # the example default is publicly known
AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE  =  true                   # set when serving behind an HTTPS reverse proxy
```


The API key check itself is a dashboard setting. Open the Endpoint page and confirm that **Require API key** is on, so requests without a valid key are rejected. It is on by default, and the dashboard shows a warning if the endpoint is reachable from a remote host without it.


Only set` AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=true` when TLS terminates in front of 9router. Over plain HTTP, the browser will not send the auth cookie back.


## Conclusion


A self-hosted router like 9router gives all your tools one endpoint and one set of credentials, and changing models only means changing the` model` string. Install it, check that` /v1/models` lists your provider’s models, then point one tool at` http://localhost:20128/v1` . Set the password and the secrets, and keep “Require API key” on, before the router leaves localhost.


## FAQs


How do I run 9router on a port other than 20128?


Start the npm CLI with 9router --port 8080 to use a custom port. When running from source, set the PORT environment variable, together with NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL pointing at the same port. In Docker, change the host side of the port mapping, for example -p 8080:20128. Every tool then needs the new base URL, such as http://localhost:8080/v1.


Where does 9router store its configuration and data?


9router stores its data in the directory set by DATA_DIR, which defaults to ~/.9router, and keeps its SQLite database at db/data.sqlite inside that directory. If JWT_SECRET is not set, an auto-generated signing secret is stored there too, at ~/.9router/jwt-secret. The official Docker image sets DATA_DIR to /app/data, so mounting a volume at /app/data persists everything.


How do I point tools on another machine at a remote 9router server?


Run npx 9router connect http://server-host:20128 on the client machine. The command starts no local server. It logs in with the dashboard password, reuses or creates an API key named cli- followed by the hostname, and writes each selected tool's config. It backs up each original config once with a .bak-9router suffix. Use --tools claude,codex to choose tools up front, and --reset to undo.


Can 9router use more than one account for the same provider?


Yes. 9router supports multiple accounts per provider and spreads requests across them using round-robin or priority-based routing. When one account hits its quota, the router switches to the next account. This is separate from combos: account rotation keeps the same model and changes the credentials behind it, while a combo moves to a different model.
